sink: caller-supplied int flows unmodified from server.py build_deep_index -> IndexManagementService.rebuild_deep_index -> _execute_rebuild_workflow -> SQLiteIndexManager.refresh_index/build_index -> ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=...), which controls how many OS worker threads are spun up to process the indexed file set
guard: partial: index_management_service.py line 182 only rejects max_workers < 1; there is no upper bound anywhere in the chain
why: max_workers is directly caller-controlled via the tool's own schema and is passed unchanged into concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor with no ceiling. Actual thread creation is additionally bounded by the number of files ThreadPoolExecutor.submit() is called for (one submit per discovered file), so exploitability depends on set_project_path first being pointed at a project with a large file count; against a large/monorepo-sized or symlink-expanded tree this lets a caller force creation of very large numbers of OS threads with a single build_deep_index call, a genuine uncontrolled-resource-consumption issue rather than a crash-on-malformed-input case.
contract: max_workers: Maximum number of parallel workers for file processing. ... Increase for I/O-bound workloads on machines with many cores.

why: server.py:488 check_temp_directory() takes no parameters at all; manage_temp_directory('check') in settings_service.py only reports/lists the server's own fixed temp/index directory, so there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

server.py:495 clear_settings(ctx) takes no data argument; SettingsService.clear_all_settings -> ProjectSettings.clear() only deletes two hardcoded filenames (config.json, legacy index.json) inside the server-computed settings_path, none of it caller-controlled.

system_management_service.py _validate_configuration_request (line 292) enforces enabled is bool, debounce_seconds is clamped to [0.1, 300], and observer_type must be one of a hardcoded whitelist ('auto','kqueue','fsevents','polling') before file_watcher_service._get_observer_class ever branches on it; additional_exclude_patterns is only stored as strings and later used purely as glob exclude filters, never executed or opened.
server.py:481 create_temp_directory() takes no parameters; manage_temp_directory('create') only creates/reports the server's own fixed temp directory.

pattern (server.py:383 -> FileDiscoveryService.find_files -> SQLiteIndexManager.find_files, sqlite_index_manager.py:213) is only translated by the module's own _compile_glob_regex (line 325, no nested quantifiers, so no ReDoS) and matched in-memory against an already-built list of project-relative file paths; it never touches the filesystem, a shell, or SQL directly.

code_intelligence_service.py analyze_file (line 35) calls self._require_valid_file_path -> ValidationHelper.validate_file_path (utils/validation.py:25), which rejects absolute paths and any '..'/'..\\' segment after normpath, then additionally verifies os.path.realpath(join(base_path, path)) starts with os.path.realpath(base_path) before the file is ever looked up, so traversal outside base_path is blocked twice.
server.py:512 get_file_watcher_status(ctx) takes no data argument; SystemManagementService.get_file_watcher_status only reads existing server-side state.
server.py:474 get_settings_info(ctx) takes no data argument; SettingsService.get_settings_info only reports the server's own settings/temp paths and config, none of it caller-supplied.

code_intelligence_service.py get_symbol_body (line 105) skips the explicit _require_valid_file_path check and joins base_path+file_path directly at line 182 (os.path.join(self.base_path, file_path)) before open(), which looks like a traversal gap; however the open() is only reached if index_manager.get_file_summary(file_path) (sqlite_index_manager.py:233) first returns a row, and that is an exact-match SQL lookup keyed on paths that were computed exclusively as os.path.relpath(abs_path, project_path) while walking project_path during indexing (sqlite_index_builder.py/json_index_builder.py), so a '..'-containing or absolute file_path can never match an existing row and the open() with the unsanitized path is unreachable in normal operation.

server.py:436 refresh_index(ctx) takes no data argument; IndexManagementService.rebuild_index only rebuilds the shallow index for the already-validated base_path using stored, non-caller-supplied exclude patterns.
server.py:502 refresh_search_tools(ctx) takes no data argument; SearchService.refresh_search_tools only re-probes shutil.which() for fixed tool names (rg/ug/ag/grep) on the existing PATH.

pattern/file_pattern (server.py:353 -> SearchService.search_code -> search/ripgrep.py, ugrep.py, ag.py, grep.py) are always run via subprocess.run with an argv list (never shell=True); every strategy appends a literal '--' separator before the pattern to stop option parsing, and file_pattern/exclude patterns are passed as separate argv elements (e.g. ['--glob', file_pattern] or '--include='+file_pattern) rather than being concatenated into a shell string, so neither argument nor command injection is possible; pagination and glob/regex syntax are also validated by ValidationHelper before reaching the strategy.

path (server.py:345 -> ProjectManagementService.initialize_project -> ProjectConfigTool.validate_project_path/normalize_project_path) is checked only for existence/is-directory and then used, by the tool's own declared purpose, as the root the server indexes and reads from for every other tool; pointing the indexer at an arbitrary directory the running process can already read is exactly the tool's advertised contract ('Set the base project path for indexing'), not a privilege escalation, since it grants no filesystem access beyond what the MCP server process already has.
